commitResults.messageTitle: Add import command for exported student CSV files
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors who move to another computer, or who deleted students by
mistake, have no way to bring students back other than typing every
profile in again with add.

Let's add an import command that reads the CSV format written by
export. Without confirm, it only previews the students to be added.
With confirm, it adds every new student to a copy of the address book
and replaces the stored book once, so a file is never half imported.

Rows are checked with the same ParserUtil rules as add and reported by
spreadsheet row number. Subjects are read in the export format, such
as Maths (Mon 09:00), so each subject keeps its lesson slot. Rows that
exactly match a stored student or an earlier row are skipped, so the
same file can be imported twice. The same student with different
details is an error, as the model allows only one such student.

CsvExporter.HEADER is made public so that import checks against the
exact header that export writes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover remaining CSV import edge cases
commitResults.messageBody:
Codecov reported three partly covered conditions in the import code.

Two were real CSV cases without tests: a file whose last row has no
line break, and lines that end with a lone carriage return. Let's add
tests for both.

The quote check in ImportCommandParser had a length guard that no
input could reach on its own. Let's replace the three conditions with
one pattern, which reads more simply and is fully tested.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep import inside the app folder and split execute
commitResults.messageBody:
The course's Data-Sandbox constraint does not allow the app to read
files outside its home folder, but import accepted any path, such as
a file on the Desktop.

Let's resolve the path against the folder TuteeDex runs from, which is
where export writes, and reject paths that lead outside it, including
.. steps and links. The UG now asks users to move the file into the
app folder, and its example no longer uses a Desktop path.

ImportCommand#execute() had grown to about 70 lines. Let's move the
row parsing, the comparison with stored students and the final add
into separate methods, keep each row's number with its student in a
small StudentRow class, and log the result of each import.

The byte order mark is now written as the \uFEFF escape instead of an

commitResults.messageTitle: Reopen with the last list view and sort order
commitResults.messageBody:
TuteeDex always opened on the normal list in the default order. Tutors
who work from a grouped or filtered view, such as list -subjects after
sort o/desc, had to type both commands again on every launch.

Let's save the last list or find command and the last applied sort in
UserPrefs, which MainApp already writes to preferences.json on close.
On startup, MainWindow runs the saved sort and then the saved view
through the normal command path, so the display and result box look
the same as when the user types them.

Commands that only show something, such as view, help, export and a
bare sort, keep the saved view. Other commands that switch back to the
normal list, such as add or delete, clear the saved view but keep the
sort. Saving the command text reuses the existing parsers, as the
filters are lambdas that cannot be written to JSON.

The preferences file can be edited by hand, so only list, find and
sort commands are run again; anything else is logged and ignored.

Also add import and this feature to the landing page feature list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match the start of name words in find
commitResults.messageBody:
find only matched whole words, so find Ale found nothing for Alex Yeoh.
Tutors who type quickly, or are unsure how a name is spelt, had to type
the full word.

Let's match a keyword against the start of every word in the name,
still ignoring case. Keywords in the middle of a word, such as ans for
Hans, still do not match, so short searches stay specific.

Closes #149.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow common symbols in subject names
commitResults.messageBody:
Subject names could only contain letters, digits, spaces and hyphens,
so tutors could not record subjects such as C++, Maths & Science or
Maths (H2).

Let's also allow + & ( ) . and apostrophes. Semicolons, commas and
slashes stay out, as they separate subjects in exported files, in the
displayed subject list and in command prefixes. Import still reads a
name with its own brackets, such as Maths (H2) (Mon 09:00), because
the day and time come from the last pair.

Closes #146.

commitResults.messageTitle: Confirm before clear deletes every student
commitResults.messageBody:
clear deleted every student, archived ones included, as soon as it was
typed. There is no undo, and its message still said "Address book has
been cleared!" from AB3.

Let's make plain clear only report how many students would be deleted,
and delete them with clear confirm, the same way import confirms. The
report does not save the data file, and any other argument is rejected
so a typo such as clear 3 cannot delete anything.

Closes #148.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop list and find from saving the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
TuteeDex replays the saved list or find command at startup. Both
commands used the default save-after-success behaviour, so if the
data file failed to load and the app started empty, the replay
wrote that empty address book over the user's file.

List and find only change the display, so make them skip the save,
like sort already does.

Add a test that list and find leave no data file behind, and write
the file directly in the invalid edit test, which used list to
create it.
Update/help window

commitResults.messageTitle: Let archive and unarchive take a displayed INDEX

of two students sharing a name, because the first match always won
(#119).

commitResults.messageTitle: Recall earlier commands with the Up and Down keys
commitResults.messageBody:
A typo in a long add or edit command meant typing the whole command
again, because the command box kept no history.

Keep the commands entered in this session. Up shows the previous
one and Down the next, and going past the newest brings back the text
that was being typed. A repeat of the last command is stored once.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the saved view while the filter is unchanged
commitResults.messageBody:
After `find Alice` and `delete 1`, the find filter stays on screen and
the list is empty. The saved view was still cleared, so the app
reopened on the full list instead of the view that was closed.

Delete and an edit with no changes keep the filter, so the index
numbers on screen do not shift. The saved view now follows the same
rule. It is cleared only when a command replaces the filter, or when
the screen leaves the subject groups for the contact list.

Model#getFilteredPersonListPredicate lets LogicManager compare the
filter before and after each command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain a reopened find view on startup
commitResults.messageBody:
A find view saved from the last session can reopen with no students on
screen, for example after the only match was deleted. With only the
"No contacts match" result shown, the user may think their data is
gone.

A restored find now shows a line saying it is the view from when the
app was last closed and that `list` shows all students. A restored
list view is unchanged, as it shows the student counts instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document when the saved view is kept or cleared
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides said every command that changes the list, such as `delete`,
reopens TuteeDex on the normal list. Delete and an unchanged edit now
keep the saved view, and a restored find explains itself on startup.

Update the UG rules, the DG implementation and alternatives, and add a
manual test for reopening after the only match was deleted.
